purpose: Apremilast is used to treat certain types of psoriasis (a skin condition that causes red, scaly patches) and psoriatic arthritis (joint pain and swelling related to psoriasis). It is also approved to treat mouth sores called oral ulcers that happen in people with Behcet's disease. It helps reduce inflammation and improve your symptoms over time.
how_it_works: Inside your body, there are certain proteins that can trigger inflammation and make your symptoms worse. Apremilast works by blocking one of those proteins called PDE4, which helps calm down the overactive immune response causing your skin and joint problems. Think of it like turning down the volume on the signals your body sends that cause redness, swelling, and pain.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are diarrhea, nausea, upset stomach, headache, and upper respiratory infections like a cold. Some people also experience vomiting or a runny nose. These side effects are often worse in the first couple of weeks but usually get better as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Apremilast may cause or worsen depression, mood changes, or thoughts of self-harm, so tell your doctor right away if you feel sad, anxious, or have any unusual mood changes. It can also cause weight loss, so your doctor will monitor your weight during treatment. Let your doctor know about all other medicines you take, since some medications can make apremilast work less effectively. It is not recommended during pregnancy, so use reliable birth control while taking it.
typical_dosing: Apremilast is taken by mouth as a tablet. You start with a low dose and gradually increase it over the first 5 days using a starter pack to help reduce stomach side effects. The usual full dose is 30 mg taken twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart. It can be taken with or without food.
